clue.text: Kick policeman, you will pay for it

parts.note: to foot something is to kick it
THE BILL (from 'the Old Bill') is British slang for the police

explanation.surface: A warning to someone tempted to kick a police officer: there will be consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BILL is British slang for the police, and also the title of a long-running British TV police drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is an idiom for paying the cost, here of whatever 'it' is.

indicators.note: letters thrown into chaos are jumbled, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Things at the front of a holiday town are in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: FRINTON (Frinton-on-Sea) is a seaside resort in Essex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Frinton is an example of an English seaside holiday town.

parts.note: something that lows, i.e. moos: an ox
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: An instruction to look further down for a place to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction and 'lower' like 'further down'; in fact a see is a bishop's diocese and 'lower' is a mooing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, so a see in the church sense.

indicators.note: an untidy, messed-up state, telling us to rearrange the letters of the words beside it

explanation.surface: An unmade, rumpled bed looking worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is worn so thin it looks tattered, a synonym of ragged.

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: Getting out of bed hurts for someone in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' reverses SORE, reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, used loosely for a lover or desire.

clue.text: Inside celebrated having exceedingly bad reputation

parts.note: in means inside
famous means celebrated

explanation.surface: A celebrity whose inner life has earned them a terrible name.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamous describes someone notorious, known widely for wrongdoing.

indicators.note: dis-covered, with the covering removed, so the answer is exposed within the words beside it

explanation.surface: A girl named Leila turns up in old folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a siren-like maiden of German legend who lured Rhine boatmen to their doom.

clue.text: More succinct legal summary about to be returned

parts.note: a brief is a summary of a case for a barrister

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for 'about' is read in reverse

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A shorter case summary, sent back for revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' reverses RE to give ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefer is the comparative of brief, meaning shorter or more concise.

indicators.note: something problematic is troubled, so the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Decorating an award in red turns out to be awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze medal is the award for third place in a competition.

clue.text: Bid of 500 to protect damaged reef

indicators.note: the outer letters surround and guard what goes inside them

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: the word reef is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A conservation offer of 500 to safeguard a damaged coral reef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid of 500' looks like an auction sum, but 'of' is a piece; 'damaged' shuffles to FERE and 'to protect' wraps the outer pair round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Offered is the past tense of offer, synonymous with bid in the sense of tendered.

parts.note: reads like a speedy courier, but in cricket a very fast bowler is nicknamed with a word for a devil, and 'wickedly' hints at that fiend

explanation.surface: Praise for an alarmingly speedy courier.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball; a demon bowler is one of fearsome pace. 'Wickedly' also suggests wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang for a ferociously quick bowler, whose deliveries seem diabolical to batsmen.

clue.text: Go to pieces after being dismissed in disturbance

indicators.note: the word for going to pieces is placed following the word for being dismissed

parts.note: in cricket a dismissed batsman is out
break means go to pieces

explanation.surface: Someone who falls apart after getting the sack, causing a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is a sudden eruption of trouble, such as rioting or disease.

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that looks a bit like an enigmatic sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a sign or badge standing for something, a synonym of symbol.

clue.text: Double corn mistakenly used in cookery

indicators.note: letters put down in error are wrongly ordered, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef who accidentally puts in twice the corn the recipe calls for.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordon bleu, French for 'blue ribbon', denotes cooking of the highest class.

parts.note: z is an unknown quantity in algebra
any means some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A mad stranger is carrying a few of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany means amusingly eccentric or wacky, a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: A bishop has the answer, redemption

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a solution is the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: A bishop holds the key to salvation.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is forgiveness of sins, the release from guilt that redemption brings.

clue.text: Splendid personality in part of unconscious mind

parts.note: super means splendid
ego means one's sense of self or personality

explanation.surface: A wonderful character hidden away in the depths of the psyche.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory the superego is the largely unconscious moral conscience of the psyche.

clue.text: Forced to include remarkable square disguise

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: made means forced, as in 'made him go'

indicators.note: worth remarking on, a hint that the word square is reworked

explanation.surface: Someone compelled to wear an extraordinary boxy costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forced' looks like the anagram signal but is the outer word; 'remarkable' shuffles to SQUERA, and 'to include' puts that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a false show or pretence, a synonym of disguise.

parts.note: a show is a stage play
off means called off or cancelled

explanation.surface: Bragging about a production being called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off is to flaunt or brag, so it matches boast as a verb.

parts.note: nature's own repeat performance: a sound coming back off cliffs or walls

explanation.surface: An unprompted repeat at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound repeats what was uttered, just as an encore repeats a performance.

definitions.meaning: a ... harbours an infection, often without symptoms, and can pass it on

explanation.surface: A vessel suspected of breeding infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier is both a type of naval vessel and a person or animal hosting a disease.

clue.text: Button's issue after info on the radio

indicators.note: the word for offspring is placed following the other part
broadcast speech is heard, not read, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: A child produced after a news bulletin about a button.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenson Button is a British Formula One world champion; 'Button's' means Button's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenson is the forename belonging to the racing driver Button.

parts.note: reads like a keen investor, but the stock is livestock and the follower walks behind the herd driving it

explanation.surface: A trader who watches share prices intently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock movements' suggests the stock market; it is cattle being driven to market.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover herds cattle or sheep along to market, following the animals.

indicators.note: moved away from where they were, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A whole big can has been taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means whole or complete, a synonym of entire.

indicators.note: the answer can be spotted sitting inside the place name

explanation.surface: Someone craving notice spotted in an English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop's Stortford is a town in Hertfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered sound used to catch someone's notice discreetly.

parts.note: sounds like a vain animal, but a pride is the collective name for a group of lions

explanation.surface: An animal with a high opinion of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A female lion lives and hunts within a pride, the social group of lions.

clue.text: More vigorous passion one with word of hesitation produced

parts.note: lust is strong passion
I is the Roman numeral for one
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: Desire that stammers out from someone hesitant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustier is the comparative of lusty, meaning healthy and full of vigour.

parts.note: the front is the face of something
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: Confronting the athlete who is ahead in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontrunner is the favourite or person currently ahead in a contest.
